newsitem.title: MEXICO: New testimony against Raul Salinas in murder case.
newsitem.headline: New testimony against Raul Salinas in murder case.

text.p: Mexican authorities have new testimony that strengthens their case against the brother of former President Carlos Salinas for allegedly plotting the 1994 murder of a top ruling party politician.

A former bodyguard to Raul Salinas has testified against him in the murder of Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) secretary-general Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, Attorney General Antonio Lozano told reporters late on Thursday.
"In our opinion, there is clearly enough evidence to condemn (Raul Salinas)," Lozano said.

Months after Carlos Salinas ended his 1988-94 presidency, police arrested Raul and later charged him with corruption, tax evasion and masterminding the murder of Ruiz Massieu, who was Raul's former brother-in-law.
Raul has denied all the charges against him.

Key to the prosecution's case against Raul is a missing former PRI deputy, Manuel Munoz Rocha. Officials believe Munoz Rocha helped Raul Salinas organize the murder of Ruiz Massieu and was then beaten to death with a baseball bat and buried by Raul to cover up the crime.

Bodyguard Antonio Chavez Ramirez, in new evidence, said he helped Raul Salinas hide Munoz Rocha's car following a meeting between Munoz Rocha and Raul a day after Ruiz Massieu was gunned down outside a Mexico City hotel on September 28, 1994.
Chavez also said Munoz Rocha called Raul Salinas several times on the day of their meeting. He said Raul Salinas shouted at his secretary to tell Munoz Rocha not to call him at home.

Officials suspect a body found recently in Raul Salinas's ranch on the outskirts of Mexico City is that of Munoz Rocha. Results of definitive DNA tests on the corpse will be released soon, Lozano said.
A close friend of Munoz Rocha, Manuel Espinoza Milo, earlier testified he last saw the former deputy on his way to a Mexico City house belonging to Raul Salinas.
Raul has denied ever meeting Munoz Rocha, saying he had not seen Munoz Rocha since their college days together.

Chavez recently strengthened Espinoza's account by testifying that the day after the Ruiz Massieu murder, Raul Salinas ordered Chavez to drive Munoz Rocha's car from a spot near Salinas's home to a more distant location, where it was later found by police. Chavez said Salinas ordered him to wear rubber gloves to avoid leaving fingerprints in the car.
"The testimonies from Manuel Espinoza Milo and now the chief bodyguard of Raul Salinas, Antonio Chavez, are overwhelming," Lozano said.
Chavez also testified he had seen Salinas and Munoz Rocha together on several occasions over the years and that Munoz Rocha called Salinas's home several times after the Ruiz Massieu murder.

Officials have never suggested a possible motive for Raul's alleged murder of his former brother-in-law. Theories range from a family dispute, a fight over illegal drug dealings and a dispute over Carlos Salinas's reforms.
